s: A company has 250 AWS accounts in AWS Organizations with all features enabled. A central operations team works from a dedicated operations account and needs a single feed of AWS Health events from all accounts, which it will route to its ticketing system. Company policy states that the management account must not be used for day-to-day operations. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
o: From the management account, turn on AWS Health organizational view and register the operations account as the delegated administrator for AWS Health. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule for AWS Health events in the operations account.
Create an IAM role in every account that the operations account can assume. Run a scheduled AWS Lambda function in the operations account that calls the AWS Health API in each account.
Turn on AWS Health organizational view in the management account and give the operations team console access to the management account.
Create an AWS Config aggregator in the operations account that collects AWS Health events from all accounts.

w.y: Organizational view gives one feed of AWS Health events for every account in the organization. AWS's best practice is to delegate it to a member account, so operations teams get the feed without using the management account; that account then receives the organization's Health events in EventBridge (task 1.4: multi-account event notifications).

o.A: Correct. One managed, central feed, delegated away from the management account.
o.B: Custom polling across 250 accounts is heavy to build and run, and the Health API needs Business Support+ or higher (or a legacy Business or Enterprise plan).
o.C: Breaks the policy against using the management account for daily operations.
o.D: AWS Config records resource configuration and compliance. It does not collect AWS Health events.
